purpose: cjson is a lightweight C library for parsing and handling JSON data.

functions.cJSON_Minify: `cJSON_Minify` edits a writable JSON buffer in place to remove whitespace and C-style comments, compacting the text. Use it only on mutable memory; `NULL` is ignored. It skips spaces/newlines and `//` or `/* */` comments, preserving other characters.
functions.cJSON_AddTrueToObject: Adds a JSON boolean `true` member to an object. Use it with a valid `cJSON` object and key name; it creates a `true` item and inserts it. On success returns the new item, otherwise deletes it and returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_IsString: `cJSON_IsString` checks whether a `cJSON` item is a string. Use it to test an item before reading `valuestring`. It returns `false` for `NULL`; otherwise `true` only when `(item->type & 0xFF) == cJSON_String`.
functions.cJSON_DeleteItemFromArray: `cJSON_DeleteItemFromArray(array, which)` removes the item at index `which` from a JSON array and frees it. It’s a convenience wrapper around `cJSON_DetachItemFromArray()` + `cJSON_Delete()`. If the index is invalid, nothing is deleted.
functions.cJSON_CreateObject: Creates a new empty JSON object (`{}`) as a `cJSON*`. Use it as a container, then add members with cJSON add functions. Returns `NULL` if allocation fails; otherwise the item’s type is set to `cJSON_Object`.
functions.cJSON_PrintUnformatted: `cJSON_PrintUnformatted` serializes a `cJSON` item into compact JSON text with no whitespace/pretty-printing. Use it when you need a transfer/storage string. Returns a newly allocated `char *`; `NULL` on failure. Free it with cJSON’s free function.
functions.cJSON_ReplaceItemInObjectCaseSensitive: Replaces an object member by key using case-sensitive matching. Use with a cJSON object, the target key, and a new item. Returns true on success; false if the object/key isn’t found or the replace fails.
functions.cJSON_PrintPreallocated: `cJSON_PrintPreallocated` serializes a `cJSON` item into a caller-provided buffer. Use it when you want no heap allocation: pass a valid buffer and its size, plus `format` for pretty/compact output. Returns 1 on success, 0 if `buffer==NULL`, `length<0`, or output doesn’t fit.
functions.cJSON_CreateNumber: Creates a new cJSON number node. Use it to build JSON values from a `double`. On success it sets `type=cJSON_Number`, stores `valuedouble=num`, and clamps `valueint` to `INT_MIN/INT_MAX` on overflow; returns `NULL` if allocation fails.
functions.cJSON_DetachItemViaPointer: Detaches `item` from `parent`’s array/object list without deleting it, returning the detached node. Use when you want to keep/reuse the cJSON item. Returns `NULL` if parent/item is NULL or item isn’t linked to parent.
functions.cJSON_AddNullToObject: Creates a `null` item and adds it to `object` under `name` in one step. Use it for object members that should be JSON null. Returns the added item on success, or `NULL` if creation/addition fails; on failure it deletes the temporary item.
functions.cJSON_malloc: `cJSON_malloc` is a thin wrapper around the allocator set via `cJSON_InitHooks`. Use it when you need cJSON’s configured malloc. It returns `global_hooks.allocate(size)` directly, so behavior depends on the installed hook (including returning `NULL` on failure).
functions.cJSON_IsTrue: `cJSON_IsTrue` checks whether a `cJSON` item is the JSON boolean `true`. Use it on a `cJSON*`; it returns `false` for `NULL` and for any item whose base type isn’t `cJSON_True` (only the low 8 bits are tested).
functions.cJSON_AddRawToObject: Adds a raw JSON value to an object under `name`. Use it when `raw` is already valid JSON text and should be inserted unquoted. On success returns the new item; on failure it deletes it and returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_AddItemToObjectCS: Adds `item` to `object` using a const key string. Use when the key is a literal or otherwise guaranteed to outlive the JSON object. It sets the string as const, so cJSON won’t free it; don’t write to `item->string` unless `cJSON_StringIsConst` is clear.
functions.cJSON_DeleteItemFromObjectCaseSensitive: Deletes a case-sensitive object member by key. Use with a JSON object and key string; it detaches the matching item from the object, then frees it via `cJSON_Delete`. If no matching key exists, nothing is deleted.
functions.cJSON_IsInvalid: Checks whether a `cJSON` item’s base type is `cJSON_Invalid`. Use it to test an item before treating it as a valid JSON value. Returns `false` for `NULL`; otherwise `true` only when `(item->type & 0xFF) == cJSON_Invalid`.
functions.cJSON_Delete:
`cJSON_Delete` frees a cJSON item and its linked subitems recursively. Use it on a root node when done. It skips freeing `child/valuestring/string` for `cJSON_IsReference` or `cJSON_StringIsConst` items, then frees the node itself.
Only call cJSON_Delete on the root of a still-valid tree or on detached standalone nodes. Do not delete a node that is still owned by another parent after it has been inserted, and do not access or delete nodes again after APIs like cJSON_ReplaceItemViaPointer have transferred ownership and freed the replaced item.
functions.cJSON_ParseWithLengthOpts: Parses JSON from a buffer with an explicit length, avoiding reliance on NUL-termination. Use `return_parse_end` to get where parsing stopped. Fails on `NULL`/0 length or parse errors; if `require_null_terminated` is set, extra trailing data is rejected.
functions.cJSON_AddNumberToObject: Adds a numeric child to a cJSON object. Use with a valid object and key name; it creates a number item, inserts it, and returns that item. If insertion fails, it deletes the item and returns NULL.
functions.cJSON_CreateIntArray: Creates a cJSON array from `int` values. Use with a valid `numbers` pointer and `count >= 0`; `count` must not exceed the input array length. Returns `NULL` on invalid args or allocation failure, otherwise an array of number items.
functions.cJSON_CreateTrue: `cJSON_CreateTrue()` creates a new cJSON value of boolean `true`. Use it when building JSON trees programmatically. It allocates a new item via `cJSON_New_Item`; on success `type` is set to `cJSON_True`, and on allocation failure it returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_CreateFalse: `cJSON_CreateFalse()` allocates a new `cJSON` item of type `cJSON_False`. Use it when building a JSON tree to represent the boolean `false`. It returns `NULL` if allocation fails.
functions.cJSON_CreateArray: Creates a new empty `cJSON` array node. Use it when building JSON arrays programmatically, then add elements with cJSON add functions. Returns a newly allocated array item, or `NULL` if allocation fails.
functions.cJSON_Compare: `cJSON_Compare` checks whether two cJSON values are equal. Use it with valid `cJSON*` nodes; it returns false if either is NULL, types differ, or type is invalid. If `a==b`, it returns true. For objects, `case_sensitive` controls key matching.
functions.cJSON_GetArrayItem: `cJSON_GetArrayItem` fetches the array element at a 0-based index. Use it with a `cJSON` array and nonnegative `index`. If `index < 0` or the item doesn’t exist, it returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_Parse: `cJSON_Parse` is a convenience wrapper for `cJSON_ParseWithOpts(value, 0, 0)`. Use it to parse a JSON string into a `cJSON*` tree. On success, free with `cJSON_Delete`; on invalid JSON, it returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_DetachItemFromArray: Detaches and returns the `which`th item from a cJSON array without deleting it. Use with a valid array and nonnegative index. If `which < 0`, it returns `NULL`; if the index is out of range, the underlying lookup yields `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_CreateObjectReference: Creates a reference wrapper for an existing cJSON object/array. Use it when you want `cJSON_Delete` to free only the wrapper, not the referenced children. If allocation fails, it returns `NULL`; it sets type to `cJSON_Object | cJSON_IsReference` and stores `child`.
functions.cJSON_CreateNull: `cJSON_CreateNull()` creates a new cJSON item of type `cJSON_NULL`. Use it when you need to build a JSON null value in a cJSON tree. It returns the new item on success, or `NULL` if allocation fails.
functions.cJSON_IsArray: `cJSON_IsArray` checks whether a `cJSON*` is a non-NULL array node. Use it before treating an item as an array. It returns `false` for `NULL` or any non-array type, `true` only when `(item->type & 0xFF) == cJSON_Array`.
functions.cJSON_CreateArrayReference: Creates a cJSON array node that **references** an existing child list, not a copy. Use it when you want an array wrapper around already-built items. If allocation fails, returns `NULL`. The referenced child is marked as `cJSON_IsReference`, so it won’t be freed as owned data.
functions.cJSON_AddFalseToObject: `cJSON_AddFalseToObject` creates a JSON `false` item and adds it to an object under `name`. Use it to set a boolean false member. On success it returns the new item; on failure it returns `NULL` and frees the item.
functions.cJSON_InitHooks: Sets cJSON’s global memory hooks. Call with `NULL` to reset to `malloc/free/realloc`. Otherwise provide custom `malloc_fn`/`free_fn`; `realloc` is enabled only when both are the defaults, else disabled (`NULL`).
functions.cJSON_AddItemReferenceToObject: Adds a reference to `item` into `object` under `string`. Use it when you want the same JSON value shared, not copied. Returns false if `object` or `string` is NULL; otherwise it wraps `item` via `create_reference` and adds it.
functions.cJSON_GetStringValue: `cJSON_GetStringValue` returns `item->valuestring` only if `item` is a JSON string; otherwise it returns `NULL`. Use it to safely read a string value after checking type (or let it do the check). It does not copy or modify the string.
functions.cJSON_AddBoolToObject: Adds a JSON boolean field to an object. Use with a valid object and key name; it creates a bool item from `boolean`, inserts it, and returns the new item. On insert failure, it deletes the item and returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_PrintBuffered: `cJSON_PrintBuffered` renders a cJSON tree to text with a preallocated buffer. Use it when you have a rough size estimate: larger `prebuffer` can reduce reallocations. `fmt=0` gives compact output, `fmt=1` pretty-prints. Returns `NULL` on negative `prebuffer`, alloc failure, or print failure.
functions.cJSON_ReplaceItemInObject: `cJSON_ReplaceItemInObject` replaces an object member by key with `newitem`. Use it on a cJSON object and a valid key string. It returns `true` on success, `false` if the object/key isn’t found or replacement fails.
functions.cJSON_CreateRaw: `cJSON_CreateRaw` creates a `cJSON_Raw` item holding a duplicated raw JSON text string. Use it when you want cJSON to store preformatted JSON without parsing it. If allocation or string dup fails, it deletes the item and returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_GetNumberValue: `cJSON_GetNumberValue` returns a number node’s `valuedouble`. Use it only after confirming the item is a number (or let it check). If `item` is not a number, it returns `NAN`.
functions.cJSON_IsObject: `cJSON_IsObject` checks whether a `cJSON` item is a JSON object. Use it to safely test a node before treating it as an object. It returns `false` for `NULL`, otherwise `true` only when the item’s base type is `cJSON_Object`.
functions.cJSON_CreateStringArray: Creates a JSON array of strings from `strings[0..count-1]`. Use with a non-NULL array and `count >= 0`. Returns NULL on invalid args or allocation failure; on any element creation failure, it deletes the whole array and returns NULL.
functions.cJSON_free: `cJSON_free` releases memory using cJSON’s current deallocator hook. Use it to free pointers allocated by cJSON or compatible allocators. It does nothing special for `NULL`; it simply calls `global_hooks.deallocate(object)`. The local `object = NULL` has no effect outside the function.
functions.cJSON_DetachItemFromObjectCaseSensitive: Detaches and returns the case-sensitive object member matching `string` without deleting it. Use on a JSON object; if found, the item is removed from the object and ownership is transferred to the caller. If not found, returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_AddArrayToObject: `cJSON_AddArrayToObject` creates a new empty JSON array and adds it to `object` under `name`. Use it when you want to build an array member in an object. On success it returns the new array; on failure it deletes it and returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_ParseWithOpts: Parses JSON from a C string. Use `return_parse_end` to get where parsing stopped, or the error location if parsing fails. If `require_null_terminated` is true, the input must end at the JSON terminator; otherwise trailing data may be allowed. Returns `NULL` on `NULL` input or parse failure.
functions.cJSON_IsFalse: `cJSON_IsFalse` checks whether a `cJSON` item is the JSON false literal. Use it on a `cJSON*` to test type. It returns `false` if `item == NULL`, otherwise `true` only when `(item->type & 0xFF) == cJSON_False`.
functions.cJSON_AddItemReferenceToArray: Adds a reference wrapper of `item` to `array`, so the original cJSON isn’t moved or corrupted. Use it when reusing an existing item in another array. Returns false if `array` is NULL; otherwise it appends a reference created from `item`.
functions.cJSON_SetValuestring: `cJSON_SetValuestring` updates the `valuestring` of a non-reference `cJSON_String`. Use it only on valid string items with non-NULL `valuestring` and input. It returns the updated string, or `NULL` for wrong type, reference, NULL args, corruption, or overlapping unsafe copy.
functions.cJSON_GetArraySize: `cJSON_GetArraySize` returns the count of linked children in a cJSON array/object. Pass the array/object node; if `array == NULL`, it returns 0. It walks `child->next` and returns the number of items as `int` (may overflow for very large sizes).
functions.cJSON_AddObjectToObject: Creates a new empty cJSON object and adds it to `object` under `name`. Use it to build nested objects. Returns the new item on success, `NULL` if creation/addition fails; on failure it deletes the temporary object.
functions.cJSON_CreateStringReference: Creates a JSON string node that **references** an existing C string, so `cJSON_Delete` won’t free it. Use when the source string’s lifetime is managed elsewhere. Returns `NULL` on allocation failure.
functions.cJSON_DeleteItemFromObject:
Deletes the first object member with the given key. Use on a cJSON object and key string; it detaches that item from the object, then frees it with `cJSON_Delete`. If the key isn’t found, nothing happens.
Yes, this crash is due to API misuse. Pass only valid, NUL-terminated key strings whose memory remains alive for the entire call. Do not pass pointers to freed or soon-to-be-freed buffers. If the key comes from temporary heap memory, call cJSON_DeleteItemFromObject before freeing that buffer, and never reuse the pointer afterward.
functions.cJSON_Version: `cJSON_Version()` returns a static, NUL-terminated string with the library version (`major.minor.patch`). Use it read-only; no args needed. Each call rewrites the same static buffer, so the returned pointer is valid until the next call.
functions.cJSON_IsRaw: `cJSON_IsRaw` checks whether a `cJSON` item is a Raw node. Use it on a `const cJSON*` to test type safely. It returns `false` for `NULL`, otherwise `true` only when `(item->type & 0xFF) == cJSON_Raw`.
functions.cJSON_CreateFloatArray: Creates a JSON array from a `float` buffer. Use with a non-NULL `numbers` pointer and `count >= 0`. Returns `NULL` on invalid args or allocation failure; otherwise each float is converted to a JSON number, and the whole array is deleted if any element creation fails.
functions.cJSON_GetObjectItemCaseSensitive: `cJSON_GetObjectItemCaseSensitive` looks up a named child in a JSON object using **case-sensitive** key matching. Use it with an object node and a key string. It returns the matching `cJSON*`, or `NULL` if `object`/`string` is invalid or no exact-case key exists.
functions.cJSON_InsertItemInArray: Adds `newitem` into an array at index `which`. Use with a valid array and non-NULL item; negative index fails. If `which` is past the end, it appends. It also rejects corrupted array links.
functions.cJSON_Print: `cJSON_Print` renders a `cJSON` item into a newly allocated, formatted JSON text string using the default global hooks. Use it on a valid `cJSON*`; free the returned `char*` with the matching allocator. If `item` is `NULL` or printing fails, it returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_ReplaceItemInArray: Replaces the array element at index `which` with `newitem`. Use only with a valid `cJSON` array and non-negative index. If `which < 0`, it returns `false`; otherwise it delegates to pointer-based replacement for the found item.
functions.cJSON_ParseWithLength: `cJSON_ParseWithLength` parses JSON from a non-NUL-terminated buffer of known size. Use it when the input may contain embedded `\0` or isn’t string-terminated. It simply calls `cJSON_ParseWithLengthOpts(value, buffer_length, 0, 0)`.
functions.cJSON_HasObjectItem: `cJSON_HasObjectItem` checks whether an object contains a member with the given key. Use it with a cJSON object and a key string. It returns `1` if `cJSON_GetObjectItem` finds the item, otherwise `0` (including missing key or NULL result).
functions.cJSON_CreateBool:
Creates a new cJSON boolean value. Pass nonzero for `true`, zero for `false`. It allocates a new item; on success `type` is set to `cJSON_True` or `cJSON_False`. If allocation fails, it returns `NULL`.
cJSON_CreateBool itself is not the cause; use it only to create a fresh node that is later inserted into exactly one parent or deleted if insertion/replacement fails. Do not reuse the same created node across multiple parents without detaching/cloning.
functions.cJSON_CreateString: Creates a new cJSON string item. Pass a C string; it allocates a cJSON node and duplicates `string` into `valuestring`. Returns the item on success, or `NULL` if allocation/duplication fails. If `string` is `NULL`, behavior depends on `cJSON_strdup`.
functions.cJSON_AddStringToObject: Adds a string-valued member to a cJSON object. Use with an existing object and key name; it creates a JSON string from `string`, inserts it, and returns the new item. On failure, it deletes the temp item and returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_GetErrorPtr: `cJSON_GetErrorPtr()` returns a pointer into the last failed `cJSON_Parse()` input at the parse error location. Use it only after `cJSON_Parse()` returns `NULL`; it returns `NULL`/0 on success. You may need to inspect a few chars before it for context.
functions.cJSON_AddItemToArray: `cJSON_AddItemToArray` appends an existing `cJSON` item to an array (or object, per comment). Use it after creating the item; ownership is transferred to `array` on success. It returns `cJSON_bool` (true/false) from the internal helper.
functions.cJSON_IsNull: `cJSON_IsNull` checks whether a `cJSON` item is the JSON null type. Use it on a `cJSON*` to test for null safely. It returns `false` if `item == NULL`, otherwise `true` only when `(item->type & 0xFF) == cJSON_NULL`.
functions.cJSON_IsNumber: `cJSON_IsNumber` checks whether a `cJSON` item is a number node. Use it on a non-NULL `cJSON*`; it returns `false` for `NULL` and for any item whose low 8 type bits aren’t `cJSON_Number`, otherwise `true`.
functions.cJSON_DetachItemFromObject:
Detaches the first object member with the given key and returns it. Use on a cJSON object, then free or reattach the returned item yourself. If `object`/key is missing or not found, it returns `NULL`.
Yes, misuse is involved. The function performs a lookup through cJSON_GetObjectItem, so the key argument must point to live memory during the call. Also ensure object member names stored in the cJSON object are not dangling: if a key is dynamically allocated, add it with cJSON_AddItemToObject (which duplicates the key) rather than cJSON_AddItemToObjectCS (which keeps the pointer).
functions.cJSON_AddItemToObject: Adds `item` to a JSON object under key `string`. Use it to build objects after creating both the object and item. It returns a `cJSON_bool` success flag; the item is attached to `object` via the given key.
functions.cJSON_IsBool: `cJSON_IsBool` checks whether a `cJSON` item is a boolean (`true` or `false`). Use it to test an item before treating it as bool. Returns `false` for `NULL` and for non-bool types; otherwise `true` if `type` has `cJSON_True` or `cJSON_False`.
functions.cJSON_CreateDoubleArray: Creates a JSON array from a `double` C array. Use with a non-NULL `numbers` pointer and `count >= 0`. Returns a new array or `NULL` on invalid input/allocation failure; if any element creation fails, it deletes the partially built array.
functions.cJSON_Duplicate: `cJSON_Duplicate` creates a copy of a `cJSON` item. Use it on an existing item pointer; `recurse=0` duplicates only the node, while `recurse!=0` also duplicates child items recursively. If `item` is `NULL`, it returns `NULL` via the internal helper.
functions.cJSON_GetObjectItem:
`cJSON_GetObjectItem` fetches a named child from a JSON object, using case-insensitive matching. Pass a `cJSON` object and key string; it returns the matching item pointer or `NULL` if `object`/`string` is invalid or no match is found.
Use this API only with a valid object and a stable key string. The compared object-entry names must also still be valid. Do not create object items with cJSON_AddItemToObjectCS unless the provided key has static or otherwise guaranteed lifetime. For dynamic keys, use cJSON_AddItemToObject so cJSON owns an internal copy.
functions.cJSON_ReplaceItemViaPointer:
Replaces `item` in `parent` with `replacement` using pointers, preserving list links and shifting later items right. Use only when `item` belongs to `parent`. Returns `false` on NULL args; `true` if `replacement==item`; updates `parent->child` if replacing first item.
Misuse: the item argument must be an existing direct child of the specified parent. Do not pass a node owned by another array/object, and do not pass the same node as both target and replacement. Before calling, obtain the target from that parent (for example via cJSON_GetArrayItem or object lookup on the same parent), ensure replacement is a newly created or detached unowned node, and if ownership is unclear use cJSON_DetachItemFromArray/Object from the old parent first, then insert/replace under the new parent.
functions.cJSON_SetNumberHelper: Helper for `cJSON_SetNumberValue`: sets a cJSON number’s `valuedouble` and clamps `valueint` to `INT_MIN/INT_MAX`. Use only on a valid `cJSON*`. If `object==NULL`, it returns `NAN` and does nothing.
